country.comment: The study focuses on the 84 municipalities of the State of Hidalgo, Mexico, within the Mexican national constitutional and regulatory framework.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 6, DHA en México y su medición; PDF p. 8, El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo

effect_estimate.comment: Purely descriptive deterministic indicator ratios and time trends from institutional datasets; no statistical hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Although official physical coverage in Hidalgo reaches 96% for potable water (66.9% inside the dwelling, 29.1% within the lot; 3.9% without water on premises) and 94% for sewerage (2020 Census), constitutional Human Right to Water (DHA) standards are breached in availability, quality, and especially affordability. Across the 84 municipalities in 2022 (REPDA concessions), average state supply is 121 L/inhabitant/day, with 60 municipalities above 100 L/inhabitant/day, 14 between 50 and 100 L/inhabitant/day, and 10 below the 50 L/inhabitant/day minimum threshold (lowest in Metepec at 8, Tlahuiltepa at 13, and Tizayuca at 14 L/inhabitant/day), alongside rationed delivery every third day (tandeo) and 458 untreated municipal wastewater discharge points contaminating water sources. Combining statutory municipal water/sewerage tariffs (2022 Municipal Revenue Laws, decrees 55–170, and CAASIM tariffs) with bottled water spending, household water expenditure exceeded the 3% UNDP affordability threshold across all 84 municipalities under both 1- and 2-minimum-wage household income scenarios: in CAASIM-served municipalities in 2022, total monthly water expenditure was 403.65 MXN (134.44 MXN tariff for 8 m3 minimum + 269.21 MXN bottled water), representing 8.95% of 1 minimum wage (up from 5.04% in 2013) and 4.48% of 2 minimum wages (up from 2.52% in 2013), reaching 12.5% in Tianguistengo, 10.5% in Nicolás Flores, and 10% in Jacala de Ledezma for 1-minimum-wage households (no 95% CIs or p-values reported).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen/Abstract; PDF pp. 11–12, El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo; PDF pp. 13–17, Análisis desde los criterios del DHA, Tables 1–4, Map 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented descriptive association/pattern) within the non-experimental design ceiling of 2. The study documents statutory municipal tariffs (decrees 55–170 and CAASIM schedules), REPDA water concession volumes, and untreated discharge counts, and links them descriptively to Human Right to Water compliance ratios, but estimates household affordability and per-capita availability from aggregate secondary indicators (imputing national MOHOMA 2017 bottled water spending and minimum-wage income benchmarks, and dividing total municipal concessions by census population) rather than directly observing household-level administrative billing, rationing, or regulatory enforcement processes.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 7–8, Materiales y métodos; PDF pp. 14–16, Tables 1–4; PDF p. 18, Conclusiones

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines municipal water/sewerage/sanitation tariff schedules and fixed-volume tariff design (BURDEN / fees: Ley de ingresos, cuotas y tarifas municipales 2022 decrees 55–170 and CAASIM tariffs), legal water concession rights across sectors/municipalities (ELIGIBILITY / property: REPDA concessions under Ley de Aguas Nacionales), weak regulatory control of untreated municipal/industrial wastewater discharges (ENFORCEMENT), and federal-state-municipal governance coordination under Constitutional Arts. 4 and 115 and CEAA (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: BURDEN, ELIGIBILITY, ENFORCEMENT, fees, property, political_coordination
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen; PDF p. 6, DHA en México y su medición; PDF pp. 7–8, Materiales y métodos; PDF pp. 10–12, REPDA concessions and discharges; PDF pp. 16–18, Tables 4, Map 4, and Conclusiones

outcome_flags.comment: Quantifies and analyzes household water affordability (>3% income threshold), per-capita water supply quantity (liters/inhabitant/day), surface and groundwater quality (DBO, DQO, SST, fecal coliforms, heavy metals / semáforo rojo), municipal water and sanitation coverage/access, and intermittent rationed supply continuity (tandeo every third day).
outcome_flags.value: affordability, service_quantity, service_quality, service_coverage, water_access, sanitation_access, service_continuity
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 7–8, Materiales y métodos; PDF pp. 11–17, Gráficas 2–4, Mapas 3–4, Tables 1–4; PDF p. 18, Conclusiones

publication_year.comment: Published in Agua y Territorio, issue 24, July–December 2024 (received 02/01/2023, accepted 23/10/2023).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: This is a legal-empirical compliance study grounded in UN General Comment No. 15, Constitutional Articles 4 and 115, Ley de Aguas Nacionales, REPDA concession registries, and Hidalgo's 2022 municipal tariff decrees (decrees 55–170), combined with deterministic descriptive municipal indicators from institutional datasets rather than an analytical cross-sectional survey or regression model; thus Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework is the best design match (note: if treated purely as a secondary quantitative descriptive municipal cross-sectional indicator study, JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies would be the closest epidemiological alternative, though no inferential statistical analysis or exposure-outcome regression is performed).
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF pp. 6–8, DHA en México y su medición and Materiales y métodos

sample_size.comment: Complete census of all 84 municipalities in Hidalgo (3,083,841 inhabitants per 2020 Census) analyzed using municipal REPDA water concessions, municipal tariff decrees, and 458 untreated municipal wastewater discharge points, alongside a 10-year annual series (2013–2022) for minimum wage and estimated household water expenditure.
sample_size.value: 84 municipalities in the State of Hidalgo (total population 3,083,841 inhabitants); 10-year annual series (2013–2022) for household water expenditure
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 7, Materiales y métodos; PDF p. 8, El agua y sus características principales en Hidalgo; PDF pp. 15–16, Tables 1–4

study_design.comment: Authors describe the study as a descriptive investigation ('investigación de carácter descriptivo') operationalized by combining constitutional/human-rights doctrinal benchmarks (DHA) and statutory municipal tariff decrees with deterministic municipal-level indicator calculations and 2013–2022 descriptive time series from secondary institutional databases (REPDA, Periódico Oficial, CAASIM, INEGI Census and MOHOMA, CONASAMI, CONAGUA SINA).
study_design.value: Descriptive legal-empirical and quantitative secondary institutional data analysis across municipalities (2020–2022 cross-section and 2013–2022 annual expenditure series) evaluating Human Right to Water compliance
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF pp. 7–8, Materiales y métodos
